# ClosureCapturedValueWrite

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="native" /> <Badge type="info" text="off by default" />

Group: [Probable bugs](/rules/#probable-bugs)

Detect a closure writing a scalar captured by value when that closure is invoked and the outer variable is subsequently read without an intervening assignment.

## Example

```php{2}
<?php
$n = 0; $f = function () use ($n) { ++$n; }; $f(); echo $n;
```

Reported:

<ul>
<li>line 2: Capture the scalar by reference when updating outer state.</li>
</ul>

## Detection

- Report a closure writing a scalar captured by value when that closure is invoked and the outer variable is subsequently read without an intervening assignment.
- Resolve builtin calls and named arguments before checking the contract. Project-local callees are considered only when their bodies or immutable summaries establish the required facts. The default is disabled; enable only when the stated intent matches the application.
- For flow-dependent conditions, require a reachable source-to-use path with no intervening invalidation. Unknown calls, ambiguous aliases or recursion cannot establish definite facts. When the proof is inconclusive, nothing is reported.

## Exceptions (no report)

- Ignore writes or transformations after unconditional termination or inside a literal false if branch; these statements cannot establish a missing update or mapped value.

- Unknown invocations, object member mutation, explicit references, and deliberate inner-local results are excluded.
- The closure uses its copy as a working local, so capturing by reference would change behavior. No report when, in reachable closure code, any of these holds:
  - the captured variable is mentioned anywhere other than as the target of a write to itself (for example echoed, interpolated, passed to a call, or captured or used by a nested function or class body);
  - the value of a write to it is consumed rather than discarded, i.e. the assignment or increment/decrement is not a whole expression statement (`while ($n-- > 0)`, `echo $n = 4`, a `for` step);
  - the closure returns a value.

  A statement-level write whose right-hand side reads the same variable (`$n = $n + 1;`, `$s .= 'x';`) is still a lost update and stays reported when nothing else reads the copy. This deliberately gives up closures that update the copy and then also read it (`++$n; echo $n;`): intent cannot be told apart there.
- Unresolved targets, incomplete required facts, suppressed findings and PHP versions lacking the referenced API or language feature produce no report. User declarations shadowing builtin names are not builtin contracts.

## Fix

No automatic fix: changing capture semantics can affect lifetime and subsequent calls.

## PHP versions

Apply only on PHP versions supporting the referenced APIs and syntax (within PHP 5.3–8.5). Builtin behavior and argument contracts follow the configured PHP version. Extension-specific calls require resolved extension API symbols; do not treat same-named application functions as extension calls.

## Options

None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

## Configure

In [`custos.json`](/guide/configuration):

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "ClosureCapturedValueWrite": {
      "enabled": true
    }
  }
}
```

## Suppress

Before the statement or declaration (or the first statement of the file):

```php
// @custos-ignore ClosureCapturedValueWrite
```
